archivedDraft.scene: Sam has limited time before a train and asks the café to change the unprepared part of an order.

sourceCards.sourceNoteInternal: In some places, mostrador is also used.

sourceCards.sourceEnglish: Can I order the coffee to go?
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: コーヒーを持ち帰りで注文できますか。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Can I order the coffee for takeout?

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: Quiero esto para llevar, por favor.
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: I want this to go, please.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: これを持ち帰りでお願いします。

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: ¿Me puede dar servilletas y una cuchara?
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: Can you give me napkins and a spoon?
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: ナプキンとスプーンをいただけますか。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Can you give me napkins and a spoon?

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: ¿Me lo puede poner en una bolsa?
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: Can you put it in a bag for me?
sourceCards.sourceNoteInternal: Lo means the item you just mentioned.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: 袋に入れていただけますか。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Can you put it into a bag?

sourceCards.sourceEnglish: Does it come with a lid?
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: ふたは付いていますか。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Does it come with a lid?

sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: 私の電車はもうすぐ出発します。

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Un viajero está en un café y mira el reloj.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: A traveler is in a café and looks at the clock.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 旅行者がカフェにいて、時計を見ています。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: A traveler is at a café and looking at a clock.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Primero pide un café con leche y un croissant en la barra.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: First he orders a coffee with milk and a croissant at the counter.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: まず、カウンターでミルク入りコーヒーとクロワッサンを注文します。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: First, at the counter, he orders a coffee with milk and a croissant.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Luego dice: Disculpe, ¿puedo pedir el café para llevar?
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Then he says: Excuse me, can I order the coffee to go?
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 次に言います。「すみません、コーヒーを持ち帰りで注文できますか。」
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Next he says: 'Excuse me, can I order the coffee for takeout?'

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: La camarera pregunta: ¿Quiere una tapa y una bolsa?
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: The waitress asks: Do you want a lid and a bag?
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: ウェイトレスさんが聞きます。「ふたと袋はいりますか。」
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: The waitress asks: 'Do you want a lid and a bag?'

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: El viajero contesta: Sí, por favor, y también necesito servilletas y una cuchara.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: The traveler answers: Yes, please, and I also need napkins and a spoon.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 旅行者は答えます。「はい、お願いします。ナプキンとスプーンも必要です。」
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: The traveler answers: 'Yes, please. I also need napkins and a spoon.'

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Después cambia el croissant, porque va a comer en el tren.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: After that he changes the croissant order, because he is going to eat on the train.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: そのあと、電車で食べるので、クロワッサンの注文を変えます。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: After that, because he will eat on the train, he changes the croissant order.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Dice: ¿Me lo puede poner en una bolsa de papel?
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: He says: Can you put it in a paper bag for me?
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 「それを紙袋に入れていただけますか。」と言います。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: He says: 'Can you put it into a paper bag?'

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Al final paga la cuenta y da las gracias.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: In the end he pays the bill and says thank you.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 最後にお会計をして、お礼を言います。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: In the end he pays the bill and says thank you.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Con su pedido en la mano, sale rápido hacia la estación.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: With his order in hand, he quickly heads out to the station.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 注文したものを手に持って、急いで駅へ向かいます。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Holding his order in his hand, he quickly heads toward the station.

japaneseSpecificFocusCandidate: Request coffee to go, ask about a lid and bag, and request utensils while heading for a train.
speakingGoalInternal: Convert part of a seated order into takeaway because your train leaves soon.
sourceConflictInternal: The unreviewed curriculum asks to convert part of a seated order, but the source Reader never establishes a seated order. Source Reader 2 already orders coffee and croissant, then Reader 3 asks to order the coffee to go; Reader 6 says the croissant order changes, without specifying the requested change until Reader 7 asks for a paper bag. Preserve these ambiguities. The archived Japanese draft invents that the order is unprepared and that staff confirms a possible change, omitting the source bill, station and fuller utensil vocabulary. The source waitress is female; a Japanese neutral staff term would lose that detail. The source does not identify a city or establish any train food policy; it says the traveler plans to eat on the train.
